title: 64 House Democrats help Republicans kill Trump impeachment effort
excerpt:
Rep. Al Green is pushing the House again to vote on impeaching President Donald Trump.

Dozens of House Democrats voted to help Republicans quash an effort to impeach President Donald Trump on Tuesday...
body_text:
Rep. Al Green is pushing the House again to vote on impeaching President Donald Trump.

Dozens of House Democrats voted to help Republicans quash an effort to impeach President Donald Trump on Tuesday.

Rep. Al Green, D-Texas, forced a vote on impeaching Trump over federal immigration officials' killing of two U.S. citizens earlier this year. The move fractured House Democrats, whose leaders have largely avoided placing an emphasis on trying to oust the president as they work to take back Congress in the November midterms.

The House voted to table the measure in a 232 to 147 vote, a maneuver to get rid of it while avoiding voting on the impeachment resolution itself.

Eighteen House Democrats voted with Republicans to table the resolution, while 46 voted "present." Nearly 150 voted to move forward with a vote on impeaching Trump.

OUTGOING HOUSE DEMOCRAT AL GREEN FILES ANOTHER IMPEACHMENT RESOLUTION TARGETING PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries was among the Democrats who voted "present" on Rep. Al Green's resolution to impeach President Trump. (Samuel Corum/Getty Images; Kyle Mazza/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Democrats walked a political tightrope with the bill, forced to choose between appeasing their anti-Trump base and appealing to moderate and independent voters by showing them they were focused on tackling Americans' everyday issues like high cost of living rather than political revenge.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and his top deputies voted "present," avoiding taking a stand on the matter while allowing Republicans to more easily scuttle the resolution.

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: DEM REBELS EXPOSE CRACKS IN JEFFRIES’ HOUSE LEADERSHIP

Jeffries said in a statement that impeachment "traditionally requires a comprehensive investigative process, the collection and review of thousands of documents, an exacting scrutiny of the facts, the examination of dozens of key witnesses, congressional hearings, sustained public organizing and the marshaling of the forces of democracy to build a broad national consensus."

Rep. Al Green, D-Texas, speaks during a news conference outside the U.S. Capitol on July 23, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

"None of that serious work has been done, with the Republican majority focused solely on rubber-stamping Donald Trump’s extreme agenda," senior House Democratic leaders said. "Accordingly, we will again vote 'present' on the motion to table the impeachment resolution as we continue our fight to make life more affordable for everyday Americans, while committing to holding the crooks accountable using every tool available to us beginning on day one."

But Green railed against Jeffries and other Democrats who did not vote to impeach Trump during his own comments to reporters on Monday.

"They will acknowledge that what the president is doing is impeachable, but they would have us wait. Well, the Constitution doesn't have a wait clause in it," Green said. "I believe that there are some Republicans and Democrats who are considering voting to protect the president. If they're not considering protecting him, that will be the effect of what they will do when they vote to either table or they vote to send this to a committee for further investigation."

CONSERVATIVES ERUPT AFTER AL GREEN MELTS DOWN DURING VIRAL CLASH: 'UNHINGED LUNATIC'

Green previously forced a vote to impeach Trump in June 2025, when 128 Democrats joined Republicans in voting to table the Texas progressive's resolution.

It could also be Green's last chance to protest Trump in the halls of Congress — he was among several Democratic incumbents to lose their primary races amid a wider rebellion by left-wing voters against their establishment.

Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

title: CC Sabathia says Yankees could do a better job helping young players handle the pinstripes: 'Different beast'
excerpt:

I...
body_text:
Opening Day is tonight, with the New York Yankees facing off with the San Francisco Giants. Colin Cowherd asks if the Yankees are under the most pressure entering this season to win a World Series.

It’s been said many times over a century: earning your pinstripes with the New York Yankees is one of the hardest things to do in baseball.

Just take Anthony Volpe’s rollercoaster career with the ballclub, which has once again become a storyline as they head toward the postseason. Through four seasons, Volpe, a former first-round pick by the Yankees, has been showered with cheers, vitriol and everything in between from the fan base whose expectations will never fall lower than World Series or bust.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

If that’s not hard for a 25-year-old to deal with, Hall of Fame left-hander CC Sabathia was even a bit intimidated by the weight the pinstripes hold when he was a free agent in 2009. He eventually signed on and became a beloved figure in Yankees lore — his No. 52 is set to be retired on Sept. 26 — but he understands it’s not for everybody.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Anthony Volpe of the New York Yankees looks on after the fifth inning against the Colorado Rockies at Yankee Stadium on Sept. 10, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images)

While speaking at his PitCCh In Foundation’s 6th Annual Golf Classic at Alpine Country Club on Monday, Sabathia suggested to OutKick that the Yankees should come up with a way to not coddle those young players from the expectations, but rather help ease their way into it.

"It’s hard to watch, right?" he said when asked about what Volpe has gone through, especially now that he’s hearing cheers again after performing well following his latest call-up. "Because he’s from here, he wants to do well. And I just watched so many young players for the Yankees, whether it’s Gary Sanchez, whether it was Miguel Andujar, whoever it is, you get a label and that’s what it is, which sucks especially for a young player. I feel like the only young player that came in and did well was [Aaron] Judge because he hit 50 homers and everybody was off his back. So, it’s hard to build up equity with the fan base when you’re so young.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"George Lombard [Jr.] just went through the same thing. He had six errors in a row, and you started hearing grumblings and all these different things. So, it’s hard to develop here as a young player and I think the Yankees need to do a better job to insulating these guys and helping them understand what it is to put on the pinstripes. There’s going to be ups and downs, you gotta cancel out the noise and go out and play baseball every single day."

Of course, it’s easier said than done in a New York market where championships, no matter the sport, are expected each time a season begins. But the only way through is forward for players like Volpe, whose ups and downs since reaching the big leagues have kept fans guessing. They see what could be, but consistency hasn’t been there for the highly touted prospect.

CC Sabathia speaks at his PitCCh In Foundation's 6th Annual Golf Classic on Monday, Sept. 14, 2026 at Alpine Country Club in New Jersey. (Cesar Nunez)

"You think about Volpe’s perseverance and determination — what else is he going to do? He’s not going to quit," Sabathia added. "This is what he wanted to do his whole life. He wanted to play baseball his whole life, and he’s been in tough situations. Baseball is a hard game, but I think he’ll be better for sure, whether he’s playing second base, whether he’s playing shortstop in the Bronx or somewhere else.

"Wherever it is, he’s talented enough to play the game. Hopefully he can do some things well and help us down the stretch. Jazz can get healthy, they can platoon. We’ll see what happens. But I’m super excited for his future, not only here but if it’s somewhere else, too."

Sabathia spent 19 years in the major leagues, where expectation was immediate for him as well coming up with the Cleveland Indians in 2001 as a 20-year-old. He felt that pressure there, and even for the half season he played with the Milwaukee Brewers.

But arriving in New York was a different story in 2009. Sabathia and the rest of his star teammates came through, though, winning the World Series that season and giving a franchise synonymous with titles its 27th to extend the MLB record.

Since then, the Yankees haven’t been able to add their 28th, making just one Fall Classic in 2024 before falling to the Los Angeles Dodgers. Sabathia hopes this could be the year the Yankees get back and see it all the way through so his squad isn’t still the last New York team to win it all.

But then again, the pressure is immense to make that happen. It’s already begun as the Yankees clinch yet another postseason berth and the chance to hoist the trophy at the end of the season.

It’s pressure Sabathia feels is found nowhere else in MLB, especially for young players trying to make a name for themselves on one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world.

Anthony Volpe of the New York Yankees is in action against the New York Mets at Yankee Stadium on Sept. 12, 2026. The Mets defeated the Yankees 12-2. (Getty Images)

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

"This is the only place it happens. If you think about anywhere else, it doesn’t happen anywhere else. You think about what Roman Anthony is going through in Boston. If that was here in New York, it would be leading Sportscenter every single day," Sabathia said.

"It's a different beast when you put on the pinstripes."

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Romanian shepards and farmers clash with police
excerpt:
Riot police have clashed with Romanian shepherds and farmers as they rioted during a protest against a ban on livestock exports due to disease.

About 2,000 people gathered to demonstrate in the capit...
body_text:
Riot police have clashed with Romanian shepherds and farmers as they rioted during a protest against a ban on livestock exports due to disease.

About 2,000 people gathered to demonstrate in the capital, Bucharest, on Tuesday against the extension of a live sheep export ban, imposed by the European Union due to the highly contagious small ruminant plague. As in other protests by farmers across Europe in recent years, the rally was encouraged and supported by far-right forces.

Violence broke out in front of the Romanian government building in Bucharest when some protesters demanding the reversal of the ban began throwing rocks, metal barriers and other objects at law enforcement.

Police responded with tear gas in a bid to disperse them. Twenty-six people were detained, riot police said in a press release.

Twenty-four demonstrators and police officers required medical attention – some for broken bones, others for the effects of the tear gas. Four were hospitalised.

The government and the opposition called on the demonstrators to refrain from violence.

The demonstration was called by farmers and shepherd groups. Protesters held banners calling on the country’s president and prime minister to resign.

Some chanted the name of far-right politician Calin Georgescu, a former presidential candidate who is standing trial for acts against the constitutional order following the annulment of the presidential elections in 2024.

Supporters of Georgescu had shared messages on social media ahead of the protest, asking people to join.

George Simion, the leader of the main far-right group in the country, the Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR), wrote on Facebook that “AUR stands with the farmers and all working Romanians”, but called on protesters to demonstrate peacefully.

The Romanian government said in a press release that the protest had “degenerated into regrettable acts of violence” and called for “calm”.

President Nicusor Dan condemned the “extremely serious” violence and “any attempt to turn a legitimate protest into street fighting” in a social media post.

Romanian shepherds had protested outside the government building at the end of July over the EU ban on live sheep exports, which expires at the end of 2026.

The country of 19 million people has been struggling for months with the highest inflation in the EU and a political crisis with no end in sight.

The pro-European government, which adopted austerity measures to rein in a high budget deficit, was brought down in a no-confidence motion in May, and a divided parliament has failed to confirm a successor.

title: NFL Week 1 proper reactions: Rams panic, Bears hype and Chargers doubts need patience after one game
excerpt: Colin Cowherd lists his power rankings entering Week 2 of the 2026/27 NFL season, including the Kansas City Chiefs making a reappearance, and the Chicago Bears climbing up the ranks after an impressiv...
body_text:
Colin Cowherd lists his power rankings entering Week 2 of the 2026/27 NFL season, including the Kansas City Chiefs making a reappearance, and the Chicago Bears climbing up the ranks after an impressive Week 1.

The NFL is officially back! All 32 teams have now played exactly one game. Yet, people are going to act like that one out of 17 games is plenty of information to inform us about how the rest of the season will go.

NFL WEEK 1 TAKEAWAYS: BENGALS FLASH CONTENDER UPSIDE, BEARS EXPLODE AND PACKERS COLLAPSE

There's arguably no bigger overreaction week on the entire sports calendar than the week between Week 1 in the NFL and Week 2 in the NFL. After months of practically zero information, we finally saw teams on the field playing games that matter.

But we must remember that Week 1 accounts for 5.9% of the entire season.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Fans and media are excited to have the NFL back, which often leads to major overreactions following Week 1. (Getty Images)

People in the sports media are going to arrive at wild conclusions based on that minuscule sample size. What if you hired a home inspector for a house you wanted to buy and the inspector came back and said, "Hey, here's 5.9% of my report on this house and nothing more. You ready to make an offer?"

But here we are, every season, making decisions based on less than 6% of the information. Nonsense. Let's take a look at some of the vast overreactions seen across the landscape and break them down.

Of course, this is a major overreaction. The Rams entered the season as favorites to win the Super Bowl, rightfully so, and it seems like everyone is quickly jumping off the bandwagon. Rich Eisen Show producer and on-air contributor Chris Brockman predicted the Rams’ "dream team" would follow the 2011 Eagles and miss the playoffs.

There are two problems with this overreaction. The first, and most obvious one, is that it was one game against a good divisional opponent in Australia. Honestly, the Rams were way too cocky going into the game and traveling across the globe 28 hours prior to kickoff was a clear miscalculation. The 49ers went to Australia a week in advance to adapt to the weather and time change.

INTRODUCING OUTKICK'S FIRST ORIGINAL ANIMATED SERIES, 'SPORTS TALK WITH CAL MCCALLISTER'

The second is that the Rams weren't really at full strength. Aaron Donald didn't play, and Myles Garrett played through a lingering knee issue and is now out for at least four games. Los Angeles didn't generate much pass rush and didn't sack Brock Purdy a single time. That's not going to continue throughout the season.

Also, sometimes a team can get caught drinking its own Kool-Aid. No team entered the season with more hype, with some calling them a "super team" where a Super Bowl seemed like the only option. If anything, Week 1's disastrous result might have been the best thing that could have happened. The Rams got an early wake-up call and I expect them to bounce back in a big way over the next few games.

The Bears obviously looked great in Week 1, dropping a team-record 59 points in a season opener. Caleb Williams showed off his athleticism and playmaking abilities throughout the afternoon, and Bears fans have reasons to be excited. Bucky Brooks posited that Chicago might average 40 points per game, which would easily set the record for points in a season.

But let's pump the brakes just a tad, shall we? First, the Panthers defense isn't exactly a juggernaut. The team gave up some big numbers last season, including 42 to New England and 40 to Buffalo. In addition, Week 1 scoring was up big across the board. Teams don't play their starters much during the preseason which puts defenses at a big disadvantage. A lot of these guys have barely hit any opponents at full speed since last season and practices have gotten much less physical due to concussion and injury concerns.

Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears put on an offensive show in Week 1 against the Carolina Panthers. (Getty Images)

Chicago also benefited from several positive luck factors. The Panthers turned the ball over three times and committed 11 penalties for 84 yards. The Bears converted all four red zone drives into touchdowns and picked up 10-of-14 third downs. Yes, that's what good offenses do, but that ridiculous efficiency is unsustainable over 17 games.

Then, there was the large number of big plays. Three different Bears (Williams, D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai) all had at least one carry of at least 29 yards and four different pass catchers (Kalif Raymond, Rome Odunze, Luther Burden, and Cole Kmet) had at least one reception that went for 20+ yards. Again, great offenses produce explosive plays, but this was an outlier. The Bears are going to be good, and the offense is going to score points, but we shouldn't set the expectation at 40 points scored per game.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Chargers looked terrible in a Week 1 upset loss against the Arizona Cardinals as nine-point home favorites. The Cardinals blocked a punt, intercepted Justin Herbert and held Los Angeles to just 117 yards of offense in the second half. Mike McDaniel’s offense was supposed to unlock even more from Herbert, but it produced only two scoring drives, and one was aided by a 48-yard pass-interference penalty.

That kind of debut makes it tempting to declare the McDaniel-Herbert pairing a failure after one game.

Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel looks on as quarterback Justin Herbert warms up before a preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers. (Getty Images)

To be clear, I'm not declaring that this team is destined for great things, but burying them after Week 1 is also a mistake. McDaniel's offense is unique, and it takes time to get used to, especially for offensive linemen. The Chargers have two stud tackles, Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt, but are breaking in an entirely new interior offensive line, including a rookie center. They made a lot of mistakes, but they will improve as the season goes along.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Remember that Tua Tagovailoa thrived under McDaniel for multiple seasons and there's no reason to think that Herbert can't have more success than Tagovailoa. I do have concerns about the team's receiver corps, since the Dolphins had Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle, but Ladd McConkey is great and if they can get moderate production from the likes of Tre Harris and Quentin Johnston along with contributions from tight ends David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden, the offense will be fine.

That all being said, the Chargers clearly had too much hype coming into the season. While I don't think they're nearly as bad as they looked against Arizona, this doesn't appear to be a team that will seriously challenge for AFC supremacy, either. The Chargers might have been overhyped, but one bad Sunday doesn’t make McDaniel the wrong coordinator for Herbert.

To close, I'm going to share a few overreactions that might not be overreactions at all:

OK, that's it for Week 1. Remember that we've still got 94% of the season to play, so don't get too excited or too disappointed. Unless you're a Dolphins, Browns or Titans fan, in which case you guys should start thinking about 2027.

title: Republican Thomas Massie proposes impeaching Pete Hegseth over Iran war
excerpt:
Congressman says defense secretary repeatedly violated constitution through his handling of Iran war

Republican congressman Thomas Massie on Tuesday proposed impeaching Pete Hegseth, saying the defen...
body_text:
Congressman says defense secretary repeatedly violated constitution through his handling of Iran war

Republican congressman Thomas Massie on Tuesday proposed impeaching Pete Hegseth, saying the defense secretary had repeatedly violated the constitution through his handling of war with Iran and the deaths of civilians in conflicts worldwide.

The proposal by Massie, an iconoclastic lawmaker who lost his primary earlier this year after Donald Trump and Hegseth urged voters to oppose him, may put House Republicans in a bind just weeks before the 3 November midterm elections, where they are defending their control of Congress.

Under the rules of the House of Representatives, the articles must be voted on by Thursday, forcing Republicans to weigh in on one of the most prominent advocates of the war with Iran, which has gone on far longer than Trump said it initially would, and grown unpopular with the public.

“By engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorization, Secretary Hegseth is breaking the law and must be held accountable,” Massie said in a statement after reading the text of his resolution on the floor of the House.

“Secretary Hegseth’s constitutional violations extend beyond the illegal war in Iran. He is abusing the power of his office to ignore congressional war powers resolutions, to kidnap foreign leaders, and to intimidate critics of the Trump administration by retaliating against them for exercising free speech. If we are to remain true to our oath to ‘support and defend the Constitution of the United States,’ Congress must not turn a blind eye to Secretary Hegseth’s unconstitutional and illegal actions.”

Massie’s resolution outlines eight alleged violation of the constitution by Hegseth, a former Fox News host and army national guard officer who as defense secretary has become a pugnacious defender of the president’s military politics. These include attacking Iran without first seeking Congress’s permission, and ignoring a war powers resolution the House and Senate approved in June that would require an end to the conflict.

The resolution also accused Hegseth of “ignoring” laws that would have minimized civilian casualties, and specifically cites a US strike on a school in Minab, Iran that killed more than 168 people. Other articles allege Hegseth violated the constitution with the “extrajudicial killings” of at least 221 people on boats suspected of carrying drugs in the Caribbean sea and eastern Pacific ocean, and of “suppressing free speech” through his retaliation against Democratic senator Mark Kelly for his criticism of the secretary.

The final two impeachment articles accuse Hegseth of violating the constitution through his involvement in the military operation that captured Venezuela’s former president Nicolás Maduro, and a bombing campaign in Yemen that began shortly after Trump returned to the White House.

Should the resolution pass, they would head to the Senate, where the Republican leadership would have to decide whether to hold a trial of Hegseth, who has maintained Trump’s loyalty even as other cabinet secretaries – including attorney general Pam Bondi and labor secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer – have been shown the door.

The articles seem likely to attract many Democratic votes in the House. Massie has previously seized on unanimous Democratic support and the razor-thin Republican majority to push through a measure that forced the release of many files related to the disgraced financier and former Trump associate Jeffrey Epstein.

title: GOP Rep Thomas Massie introduces 8 articles of impeachment against War Secretary Pete Hegseth
excerpt:
Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., introduces articles of impeachment against Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on the House floor on Tuesday, Sept. 15, 2026.

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., introduced a resolution t...
body_text:
Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., introduces articles of impeachment against Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on the House floor on Tuesday, Sept. 15, 2026.

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., introduced a resolution to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and read eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth on the House floor Tuesday.

Massie formally entered a resolution to impeach Hegseth for "high crimes and misdemeanors" on the House floor for, among other things, allegedly violating the War Powers Resolution of 1973 in Iran and for his role in the operation that led to former Venezuelan dictator Nicolas Maduro's capture and extradition.

The first three of the eight articles of impeachment Massie introduced accused Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution of 1973, arguing that Hegseth's Department of War is "waging the Iran war despite no declaration of war, statutory authorization, attack on the United States, or imminent threat."

His first article seeks to establish "that the war was unlawful from its inception." The second article claims that Hegseth disobeyed Congress after both the House and the Senate directed the removal of troops from Iran. The third article claims that Hegseth is "continuing hostilities in Iran after expiration of the War Powers Resolution’s 60-day termination period and any potential 30-day withdrawal period."

4 HOUSE REPUBLICANS REBEL AGAINST TRUMP, VOTE WITH DEMS TO BLOCK IRAN WAR POWERS

U.S. Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., introduces a resolution to impeach War Secretary Pete Hegseth in connection with the U.S. conflict with Iran on Sept. 15, 2026. (House TV/Handout via REUTERS)

The fourth and fifth articles accuse Hegseth of refusing to minimize civilian casualties and engaging in extrajudicial killing, with the latter charge accusing Hegseth of "replacing maritime law enforcement with unauthorized lethal military targeting of suspected drug traffickers" during operations striking suspected narcotraffickers in the Caribbean Sea.

REP SETH MOULTON SAYS HEGSETH IS 'GUILTY' OF WAR CRIMES, LINKS HIM TO NAZIS TRIED DURING WORLD WAR II

Also related to military action in the Caribbean and South America, Massie's seventh article accuses Hegseth of the "Kidnapping of a Sovereign Foreign Leader" for his role in Operation Absolute Resolve, the January mission in which U.S. Special Forces apprehended and extracted former Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores from Caracas. Massie's article condemns Hegseth for doing so "without constitutional or legal authority."

War Secretary Pete Hegseth speaks during a press conference on U.S. military action in Iran at the Pentagon in Washington, D.C., on Mar. 2, 2026. (Brendan Smialowski/AFP/ via Getty Images)

Article six accuses Hegseth of using his authority to suppress the free speech of Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., by retaliating against the senator for his video in which the senator joined a group of other lawmakers in a video which critics claimed encourage active military members to disobey lawful orders.

The final article charges Hegseth with carrying out unlawful orders in Yemen. The article "charges Secretary Hegseth with initiating Operation Rough Rider without congressional authorization or an imminent threat to the United States, while also violating war powers reporting requirements. It further addresses extensive civilian deaths and unlawful strikes on civilian objects, rescuers, and other protected persons."

After reading out his articles for over an hour on the House floor, Massie closed out his introduction.

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., arrives for a House vote on the funding bill to reopen the government on Feb. 3, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

"In all of this, Secretary Hegseth abused the powers entrusted to him as Secretary of Defense by subordinating the constitutional limits on the use of military force and the laws governing the conduct of hostilities to his own policy objectives," Massie said.

Massie also added that Hegseth "has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to civilians, the lawful conduct of United States military operations, the integrity and credibility of the United States Armed Forces and the Constitution, if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties, and the rule of law.

This, Massie said, "warrants impeachment and trial, removal from office and disqualification to hold and enjoy any office of honor, trust or profit under the United States."

Fox News Digital contacted Massie's office and the Pentagon for further comment.

title: India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets to seal T20 series
excerpt:
Sanju Samson scored 57 off 22 balls as India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets to clinch their three-match T20 series with a match to spare on Tuesday.

Samson hit four sixes and seven fours en route ...
body_text:
Sanju Samson scored 57 off 22 balls as India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets to clinch their three-match T20 series with a match to spare on Tuesday.

Samson hit four sixes and seven fours en route to his first half-century since this year’s T20 World Cup final – where he was named player of the tournament.

His opening partner Abhishek Sharma scored 39 off 19 balls – including four sixes – as the duo amassed 88 off only 38 balls.

India finished with 163-3 in 14.5 overs. It had won the first T20 by seven wickets as well, at the same venue on Sunday.

Afghanistan is playing host in this series, in a unique arrangement, and for the second game running, it finished with an under-par score after India won the toss and opted to field.

All-rounder Nitish Reddy picked 3-24 in three overs as Afghanistan was restricted to 159-8 in 20 overs.

Samson and Sharma set a hectic pace as India raced to 82-0 in the powerplay. Afghanistan used spin in the powerplay as compared to the first game, but to no avail.

Rashid Khan came on after the powerplay, getting the breakthrough in the seventh over, as Sharma was out caught at deep midwicket.

Samson carried on to reach his seventh T20 half-century off 20 balls. Khan picked a second wicket in the seventh over, as Samson holed out to long-off.

But India had powered its way to 100 in 7.1 overs – joint second-quickest for them since 2024.

Skipper Shreyas Iyer was Khan’s third victim, out caught at slip, but Ishan Kishan (38 not out) and Tilak Varma (15 not out) polished off the remaining runs without any bother.

Earlier, put in to bat, Afghanistan made another poor start. Rahmanullah Gurbaz fell for a second consecutive duck, this time to Arshdeep Singh.

Skipper Ibrahim Zadran scored 37 off 33 balls to make sure Afghanistan didn’t lose too many wickets in the powerplay again.

But the “hosts” slid from 59-2 to 100-6 in the middle overs and lost their base as Reddy picked two wickets. Afghanistan only managed to recover thanks to a 48-run partnership off 28 balls between Rashid Khan and Mohammad Nabi.

Khan hit 28 off 16 balls with three fours and a six, while Nabi scored 20 off 14 balls.

title: Egypt’s el-Sisi meets MBS, backs Saudi call for secure Red Sea navigation
excerpt: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi has backed Saudi calls for secure and unhindered navigation in the Red Sea during a meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Cairo, according to a state...
body_text:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi has backed Saudi calls for secure and unhindered navigation in the Red Sea during a meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Cairo, according to a statement by the Egyptian presidency.

Sisi met the crown prince, known as MBS, on Tuesday as part of a Saudi delegation that included Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and other senior officials.

The statement affirmed that “relations between Egypt and Saudi Arabia can only be exemplary within the Arab framework, and that the security of Saudi Arabia and the Gulf states is an integral part of Egypt’s national security”, while also emphasising efforts to achieve a sustainable political solution to the Yemen conflict. The Saudi-backed Yemeni government has lost key territories including coastal areas vital for oil shipping to the Iran-aligned Houthis in recent days.

MBS emphasised the importance of secure navigation in both the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Red Sea, according to the Saudi Press Agency.

The visit by Saudi leaders comes as Yemen’s Houthi rebels have captured Mocha port and effectively control the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

Despite Houthi assurances that maritime traffic in the Red Sea will not be affected, Saudi-linked ships have been targeted by the group in recent months.

The sharp decline in Red Sea transit affected Egypt’s economy, which relies heavily on Suez Canal tolls as a key source of foreign currency.

Egypt lost approximately $7bn between 2023 and 2024, or about 60 percent of the Suez Canal’s revenues, according to the Suez Canal Authority.

Despite Egypt’s assurances, the country has so far avoided military action to stop the Houthi disruption of tanker traffic in the Red Sea.

title: Police crack down on protests against constitutional change in DR Congo
excerpt:
Protests in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have spurned violent clashes as police cracked down.

Police fired tear gas as hundreds of people protested in the capital Kinshasa on Tuesday ag...
body_text:
Protests in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have spurned violent clashes as police cracked down.

Police fired tear gas as hundreds of people protested in the capital Kinshasa on Tuesday against proposed constitutional changes that critics worry could allow President Felix Tshisekedi to seek a ‌third term in power. The political unrest adds to DRC’s struggles as it faces a rapidly spreading Ebola outbreak and ongoing conflict in the east of the country.

At least 10 people were arrested during the confrontations, with demonstrations also taking place in the cities of Lubumbashi – a major mining centre in the southeast of the country – and Uvira, despite restrictions imposed by authorities.

The protests were part of a nationwide day of action called by the “C64” coalition, which was forged by opposition forces in a bid to defeat Tshisekedi’s attempt to change the constitution.

“Many of our activists were unfortunately and arbitrarily arrested,” said Mohamed Eyenga of the Envol opposition party, a senior figure in the C64 coalition, according to the AFP news agency.

“We were taken aback by the large deployment of the army and police to prevent this peaceful demonstration,” he said.

However, the provincial police commander, General Blaise Kilimbalimba, insisted that “peaceful” demonstrators had not been arrested.

Congo’s constitution currently limits presidential terms to two five-year increments.

DRC’s parliament adopted a bill in June allowing constitutional changes to be put to a ⁠referendum, and members of Tshisekedi’s coalition have backed changes that would allow him to remain in office.

Opposition parties and the powerful Catholic Church have condemned the proposal.

The unrest comes three weeks after Tshisekedi announced plans for a national dialogue, bringing together opposition parties, civil society groups and religious leaders.

However, the discussion would exclude the M23 and other rebel groups that control parts of eastern DRC. Fighting over the resource-rich region has persisted for decades, and flared up once more in 2024.

Kinshasa accuses Rwanda of supporting the M23 rebels – an allegation that Kigali denies. Key commitments under a precarious peace process remain unresolved.

Officials from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Rwanda are due to reconvene in Geneva, Switzerland on September 16 and 17 for talks on the implementation of the 2025 Washington Accords.

The conflict has complicated the DRC’s bid to suppress the Ebola outbreak, which is now the world’s worst on record.

The disease has spread across conflict-plagued, remote eastern and northern regions, where armed groups have roamed for decades, the presence of the state is weak, and health infrastructure is largely lacking.

title: Georgia city removes 23-year-old mayor after sexting and municipal funds scandal
excerpt:
Jayden Williams of Stockbridge alleged to have made inappropriate texts to teen and using city funds improperly

City leaders in a suburb outside Atlanta have voted to remove the youngest mayor in the...
body_text:
Jayden Williams of Stockbridge alleged to have made inappropriate texts to teen and using city funds improperly

City leaders in a suburb outside Atlanta have voted to remove the youngest mayor in their community’s history amid allegations of questionable spending of municipal funds and inappropriate communications with an 18-year-old high school student.

Over the weekend, the Stockbridge, Georgia, city council voted to remove Jayden Williams, 23, from office after an hours-long hearing into allegations that included inappropriate exchanges with an 18-year-old in high school, improper purchases on a municipal government-issued credit card and mistreatment of employees.

Williams took office in January after defeating incumbent Anthony Ford in an election two months earlier.

According to local news outlets, an investigation into Williams preceding his removal examined his communications with an 18-year-old high school student.

Williams at one point reportedly offered the teenager a city-backed internship and mentorship while also asking if they could be “friends with benefits”, a term implying a casual rather than a committed sexual relationship. Williams reportedly added, “This better stay between us too,” according to the outlet.

During the council hearing, lawyer Robbie Ashe, who was representing Stockbridge investigators, asked Williams: “Is getting nude photographs via text message so unremarkable to you that you don’t remember when you get them?” NBC reported.

Williams replied, “It’s not memorable nor is it abnormal for somebody my age.

“That’s not abnormal for somebody my age.”

The communications in question began shortly after Williams’ election victory and were carried out on Williams’ personal phone, Atlanta News First reported. They included sexually suggestive messages and explicit photos.

Other allegations against Williams involved his use of a city-issued credit card. According to Atlanta News First, the purchases included $35.79 for movie tickets, $63.83 at a Polo Factory store and $322.92 at Pandora.

Williams said his use of the city-issued credit card was accidental because it is the same color and looks like his personal card. “Nobody said anything to me at the time,” he said, adding that he had reimbursed the city, according to Atlanta News First.

Investigators also alleged that Williams created a hostile work environment, including changing the locks on his office and requiring staff to slide documents underneath the door. They also accused him of shouting at staff members and allegedly threatening an interim city clerk that she would never be permanently appointed, the outlet reported.

During the hearing, Williams denied ordering the locks to be changed and said keys often jammed in them, according to Atlanta News First.

Stockbridge officials discussed Williams’ removal in a statement that said: “The city … has taken formal action concerning the office of mayor following proceedings conducted pursuant to applicable city processes. As a result of that action, the mayor has been removed from office.”

After the hearing, Williams’ attorney, Robert Kenner, said the council’s removal of his client “was very disappointing”, NBC reported.

“I don’t believe that it was based on any evidence.”

Meanwhile, interim mayor Elton Alexander said Williams’ fate stemmed from the findings of whom he described as an independent investigator, Richard Hyde.

“Removing Stockbridge mayor Jayden William from office was a tough decision,” Alexander said. “It brings a fair and equitable close to multiple troubling accusations that were investigated and verified by [Hyde]. The results of the investigation demanded we act.”

Williams is not the only young mayor to have been met with legal or political trouble.

Tyrin Truong was elected mayor of Bogalusa, Louisiana, in 2022 at 23 years old and was arrested in January 2025 in connection with a drug-trafficking investigation. He has pleaded not guilty to multiple charges, including malfeasance and theft, and in January 2026 announced a re-election bid.

title: Kash Patel reveals FBI's capture of all 10 members of Most Wanted fugitive's list during hearing
excerpt:
Kash Patel, testifying to the Senate Judiciary Committee, reveals that the FBI has caught all 10 of the FBI's 10 Most Wanted fugitives.

The FBI has apprehended all 10 members of the FBI's Most Wanted...
body_text:
Kash Patel, testifying to the Senate Judiciary Committee, reveals that the FBI has caught all 10 of the FBI's 10 Most Wanted fugitives.

The FBI has apprehended all 10 members of the FBI's Most Wanted list during President Donald Trump's second term, FBI Director Kash Patel revealed during an appearance in front of the Senate Judiciary Committee on Tuesday.

Sen. Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, during his opening statements as the committee's chairman, lauded Patel and the FBI for their work in capturing nine of the ten most wanted fugitives on the FBI's top ten list.

Patel, during his opening remarks, corrected Grassley, revealing that his agency had just this past weekend caught the tenth fugitive.

"Mr. Chairman, I'm proud to announce today, and I hate to correct you, we haven't captured nine of the top ten most [wanted] individuals on our list. We've captured ten," Patel said.

FBI CAPTURES TOP TEN MOST WANTED FUGITIVE WITH ALLEGED SINALOA CARTEL TIES, PATEL SAYS

FBI Director Kash Patel arrives to testify during a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing in the Hart Senate Office Building on Sept. 15, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

"Just this past weekend, we captured a thug down in Venezuela who was on our most wanted list and on the run for years. He has been captured, apprehended, and is on his way back to the United States of America. That's ten of ten. Nobody in the FBI history has done that," Patel said.

HIGHEST-RANKING TREN DE ARAGUA MEMBER EVER EXTRADITED TO US SET TO APPEAR IN HOUSTON COURTROOM: DOJ

"We, the FBI, captured more than two and a half times the number of the top ten most wanted fugitives on the FBI's list from the prior administration," he also said.

While Patel did not say the name of the fugitive during the hearing, the FBI earlier revealed exclusively to Fox News Digital that the 10th capture was that of Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre, the FBI's first ever "cyber fugitive."

Aguirre led "a large international conspiracy to steal millions of dollars from financial institutions in support of the Tren de Aragua, through an ATM jackpotting scheme since at least 2024," the FBI told Fox News Digital.

Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre's FBI Ten Most Wanted profile (FBI Media)

In addition to a clean sweep of the top ten fugitives, Patel also revealed that his FBI has also captured six of the top ten most wanted fraudsters on the top ten fraudsters list, a compilation his FBI created during the current administration.

FBI TOUTS 6,000 ARRESTS, 44% HOMICIDE DROP ONE YEAR INTO TRUMP'S DC CRIME CRACKDOWN

Patel also outlined the broader progress the Trump administration has made towards making the U.S. safer.

"On top of that, we've captured six of the most wanted fraudsters around the world, taking the murder rate down 20 points is no easy effort. It requires a team left state, local and international partners. This includes results in cities like Baltimore, which retreats its lowest mid-year homicide numbers in recorded history," he said.

TRUMP’S LAW-AND-ORDER BLITZ MARKS ONE YEAR WITH EYE-POPPING HAUL OF SUSPECTS, GUNS IN BLUE CITY

FBI Director Kash Patel is sworn in to testify during a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing in the Hart Senate Office Building on Sept. 15, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

"This year in Memphis, we accomplished a 50% reduction in homicide for a city that had the highest per capita homicide rate in the country, thanks to the president's task force. And right here in Washington, D.C., we are on track to have the lowest homicide numbers since 1990," Patel added.

Fox News Digital contacted the FBI for further comment.

Fox News Digital's Bonny Chu contributed to this report.

title: British woman abducted in Malawi, police say
excerpt:
Police have offered a reward for details that could help find Nusrat Osman

Police in Malawi are investigating the kidnapping of a British national who was abducted in the southern African nation's ma...
body_text:
Police have offered a reward for details that could help find Nusrat Osman

Police in Malawi are investigating the kidnapping of a British national who was abducted in the southern African nation's main city, Blantyre.

Nusrat Osman, 47, was seized at around 12:30 local time on Friday by four men who had been travelling in a grey Nissan Dualis, according to a police statement.

The authorities have offered a reward of more than $17,000 (£12,600) for "credible information" that could lead to the rescue of the mother of two young children and the prosecution of the perpetrators.

Osman was reported to have been working for a local auditing firm.

A Malawi news outlet reported that Osman's husband was in anguish about the disappearance.

"I don't know where she is or how she is. My wife is an auditor and I have no issues with anyone," he was quoted by Nyasa Times as saying.

Police said the motive behind the abduction was unknown and that so far the kidnappers have not contacted the victim's family or the authorities.

The UK Foreign Office told the BBC that it was aware of reports that a British national had been abducted in Malawi and was in touch with local authorities.

Go to BBCAfrica.com, external for more news from the African continent.
